exposure: Patients with vs. without unintended uterine extension during primary cesarean delivery
unintended uterine extension in cesarean delivery
trial of labor after cesarean delivery (TOLAC)
Unintended uterine extension during primary cesarean delivery
outcome: Uterine scar disruption (rupture or dehiscence) at subsequent trial of labor after cesarean delivery (TOLAC)
cohort: 7,199 patients who underwent a trial of labor after cesarean delivery between 2005 and 2021
finding: While unintended lower-segment uterine extension during primary cesarean delivery was not associated with an increased risk of uterine scar rupture in a subsequent trial of labor, it was linked to higher rates of TOLAC failure.
mod_finding: Unintended uterine extension during primary cesarean delivery was not associated with an increased risk of uterine scar rupture in a subsequent trial of labor, but it was linked to higher rates of TOLAC failure.
